title: Blueprint Ballistics

selected_categories.reasoning: The defining player action is drawing lines to solve trajectory problems. The orb is influenced indirectly through player-authored geometry rather than direct avatar control.
Gravity, collision normals, rebound angles, damping, and wall bounces are central to success. Understanding momentum and reflection is part of the intended play skill.
The run continues until the orb falls out of bounds, so play is framed as survival under increasing self-created spatial complexity and reactive correction.
A large part of the appeal comes from luminous rails, particles, glow effects, and pleasant score feedback. The audiovisual polish supports a tactile, satisfying toy-like loop.
This is only a weak fit, but it shares endless score-chasing structure and continuous failure-ends-run pacing. It lacks lane movement and forward auto-run, so this remains a distant fifth match.

uncertainty_notes: The category universe does not contain a direct 'arcade physics score attack' label, so the ranking favors the closest mechanical analogs.
The fifth slot is especially low confidence because the game is not a conventional runner and could also loosely fit categories like Meta game or ASMR relaxing game depending on interpretation.
No level progression, resource economy, combat, or narrative framework is present in code.
